To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

herpes virus-specific regulatory T cells (Ts cells) are induced in a manner dependent upon the form of the virus antigen (membrane or nonmembrane associated), the multiplicity of infection, and the length of incubation with the virus, and that these Ts cells have different requirements for the expression of suppressor function.
the induction requirements and effector function of HSV-specific Ts differ.
two types of HSV-specific suppressor T cell populations are induced in mice tolerant to HSV-infected SC.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the regulation of the immune response to herpes simplex virus.
the regulation of cell-mediated immunity to herpes simplex virus (HSV).

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the two types of suppressor T lymphocytes are induced by different forms of viral antigen, and that the effector function of the two types of cells is different.
the induction requirements and effector function of Ts-eff and Ts-aff are different.

the Ts-eff are induced in vivo by the expression of nascent HSV antigents on the surface of infected SC, and that the Ts-aff are induced in vivo either by the expression of HSV antigens adsorbed to the surface of SC or by the expression of these antigens on the surface of the SC themselves.

HSV-specific Ts-eff are induced in vivo by the same viral proteins that are required for the induction of HSV-specific cytotoxic T cells.
